extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology for open scientific research in computational linguistics, providing metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, structured full texts, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi; Yanxia Qin; Benjamin Aw; Niranjana Unnithan; Min-Yen Kan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built by crawling PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology, removing PDFs longer than 50 pages, extracting full text from PDFs with GROBID, extracting figures and tables with PDFFigures, and enriching records via the Semantic Scholar Graph API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some fields are only available for a subset of papers; for example, only 16.8% of papers have an arXiv paper ID. Full-text extraction also fails mostly for papers between 2000 and 2015.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources are ACL Anthology PDF documents and metadata, plus additional information from the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed; citation networks were constructed using internal and external citations; records were linked to Semantic Scholar and some automatically detected fields such as language and topic were added.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDFs were processed with GROBID for full-text extraction into S2ORC-JSON format, and figures/tables were extracted separately using PDFFigures.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For topic classification, the authors crawled published papers from online CL conferences between 2020 and 2022 together with their topics from conference websites, aligned them with ACL OCL, and used the resulting 2,545 documents with 21 topics as training and testing data. The dataset also includes model-predicted silver topic labels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper analyzes topic-label quality through model evaluation and notes that predicted topics are silver data; two errors in a case study were attributed to insufficient training samples and overlap with other topics.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID, PDFFigures, langdetect, BART-large-MNLI, SciBERT, SPECTER
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates by downloading and processing newly added ACL Anthology papers, identified via URL changes; the authors plan yearly updates to keep OCL current.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The corpus is intended to accelerate scientific progress, promote reproducibility, support open research in computational linguistics, and draw attention to emerging topics such as Ethics of NLP and declining underrepresented topics.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The corpus is biased toward peer-reviewed, open-access ACL Anthology papers in computational linguistics, excludes other sources, and topic analyses may be biased toward dominant topics such as machine translation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The corpus is limited to ACL Anthology peer-reviewed open-access CL papers and is not comprehensive; full-text quality is constrained by PDF extraction errors; only open-source PDF-to-text tools were used; the corpus is largely unlabeled for task-specific annotations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Open research in computational linguistics; temporal topic trend analysis; topic analyses and topic-aided tasks; document-level terminology detection; coreference resolution; pre-training or fine-tuning scientific language models; summarization; related work generation; section-specific information extraction; historical language change analysis; knowledge graph construction; multimodal research tasks.

name.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain.

description.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. Integrating and enhancing the previous versions of the ACL Anthology, the ACL OCL contributes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs and additional structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to a large knowledge resource (Semantic Scholar).
